statement: A consortium of 10 banks led by Goldman Sachs, SMBC, Barclays, BNP Paribas and Bank of Nova Scotia is lending $22 billion to the Blackstone-Alphabet venture Crux AI, secured on the chips themselves and on customer contracts.
why: Large banks accepting AI accelerators as collateral shows the credit channel that funds non-hyperscaler compute buildouts is still wide open, which is what lets marginal buyers keep ordering.

impact.mechanism: Chip-backed debt at this scale expands purchasing power for accelerator capacity generally, but this tranche funds Google TPUs rather than merchant GPUs, so it also finances a competing accelerator.

evidence.excerpt: will be backed by the value of those chips and Crux AI's customer contracts

confidence.basis: Two-step secondary chain - Investing.com citing Reuters citing Bloomberg's original report - with no loan documentation disclosed and no tenor stated.

dispersion: $22 billion of bank debt alongside Blackstone's initial $5 billion equity investment; syndication to more lenders still in progress and the debt may later be refinanced in the investment-grade bond market.
